title: Deferred Execution: JCL → JES
description: Submit a job and trace the execution chain. Identity binding, JES scheduling, deferred trust.

steps.title: What is JCL?
steps.expected: Understand the three parts of a JCL job: JOB, EXEC, DD.
steps.hint: JOB card = identity + accounting. EXEC = program to run. DD = data definition.

steps.title: Create a Test Job
steps.screen:
EDIT - HERC01.JCL(TESTJOB)
Command ===> 
****** ********************************* Top of Data *
000001 //TESTJOB JOB (ACCT),'TEST',CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=X
000002 //STEP1   EXEC PGM=IEFBR14
****** ******************************** Bottom of Data
steps.expected: Create a simple JCL member with IEFBR14.
steps.hint: Use RFE option 2 (Edit) or the EDIT command. Type SUB to submit.

steps.title: Submit the Job
steps.screen:
READY
SUB 'HERC01.JCL(TESTJOB)'
IKJ56250I JOB TESTJOB(JOB00123) SUBMITTED
READY
steps.expected: Job submitted to JES input queue with assigned job ID.
steps.hint: Note the job number (JOB00123). JES assigns a unique ID to every submitted job.

steps.title: Check Job Status
steps.screen:
READY
STATUS TESTJOB
IKJ56192I JOB TESTJOB(JOB00123) ON OUTPUT QUEUE
READY
steps.expected: Job appears in output queue after execution.
steps.hint: STATUS shows: ON INPUT QUEUE (waiting), EXECUTING, ON OUTPUT QUEUE (done), or NOT FOUND.

steps.title: View Job Output
steps.screen:
READY
OUTPUT TESTJOB PRINT(*)
1                       J E S 2  J O B  L O G
0 21.15.32 JOB00123 $HASP373 TESTJOB  STARTED
  21.15.32 JOB00123 IEF403I TESTJOB - STARTED
  21.15.32 JOB00123 IEF404I TESTJOB - ENDED
0 21.15.32 JOB00123 $HASP395 TESTJOB  ENDED
------ JES2 JOB STATISTICS ------
  0 CARDS READ
  24 SYSOUT PRINT RECORDS
IEF142I TESTJOB STEP1 - STEP WAS EXECUTED - COND CODE 0000
READY
steps.hint: COND CODE 0000 = success. The OUTPUT command displays and deletes job output.

steps.title: Deferred Trust Implications
steps.screen:
Security Analysis: Deferred Execution

Key insight: JCL runs LATER under the submitter's identity.

Timeline:
  1. You submit JCL at 09:00
  2. JES queues it (identity: HERC01)
  3. Job executes at 09:05 (still identity: HERC01)
  4. Output waits for you (owned by: HERC01)

Attack vector:
- Inject JCL into a trusted user's input stream
- Job runs with THEIR identity, not yours
- Deferred = harder to detect in real-time

This is the mainframe equivalent of a cron job injection.
RACF/RAKF logs capture submission time, not execution time.
steps.expected: Understand why deferred execution creates unique security risks.
steps.hint: Unlike interactive commands, batch jobs run asynchronously - detection and attribution are harder.
